title: How NOT to Plan a Destination Wedding

slides.quote: We were able to just be fully present and enjoy every moment knowing we were in great hands.

slides.body:
Start with your budget, your guest count and your style.
Count your events first. The room is the easy part.

slides.lead:
Do not assume a destination
wedding is cheap.
slides.body:
You are funding a whole celebration, not a ceremony.
Flights, stays, attire, rings, venue, guest meals,
every event, the honeymoon. Guests book their own travel.

The cheapest quote is the one with the least in it.
A cheap decision costs more later, in stress,
compromises and quality you cannot fix on the day.

slides.lead:
Do not compare Bali
options on price alone.
slides.body:
Compare the whole experience. The venue and the
setting, the service, how your culture is handled,
and the days around the day. Not the number.

slides.lead:
Do not book before you
know what is included.
slides.body:
Ask what is in the price and what is not.
Meals, venue rules, guest logistics, staffing,
overtime, corkage. Get it in writing before you pay.

slides.lead:
Do not hire anyone
you have not checked.
slides.body:
Check they are a legal business with a reputation
you can find yourself. Ask for a wedding they ran
at your size, and meet the team who runs your day.

slides.lead:
Do not pick a planner
on experience alone.
slides.body:
The most weddings behind them is not the same
as the most attention on yours. Ask how much
they are willing to change for you.

slides.lead:
Do not plan only
for the wedding day.
slides.body:
A welcome event before it. A recovery day after it.
A honeymoon at the end. Guests who fly this far
stay for days, and every day needs a plan.

slides.lead:
Do not wait to get
expert advice.
slides.body:
The earlier you get clarity on budget, venue and
what is actually possible, the more of your
shortlist is still available to you.

items: Count your events before you look at venues
Budget for the whole celebration, not the day
Agree one clear process with both families
Meet the person who runs your day
